sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (fill in the blanks, true/false, one word or phrase, match).

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: Sufis were organised into ______ orders or silsilahs. These were named after their founders Chishti, Suhrawardi, Qadiri and ______.
Fill in the blanks: The Bhakti and ______ movements emerged in medieval India. Both held that ______ is supreme and all men are equal to him.
Answer in a phrase: (a) Why did aristocrats live in great luxury during the medieval period? (b) Why did the Sultan outmatch all aristocrats in style and luxury?
questions.answer: (a) To show their wealth and status and to imitate the ruler; (b) to maintain his superiority and status and show he was different from others.

questions.q: Answer in a phrase: (a) Name a nirguna Bhakti poet. (b) Name a saguna Bhakti poet.
questions.answer: (a) Kabir or Nanak. (b) Tulsidas or Surdas.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (a) The names of the Khalifa and the Sultan were read in the ______. (b) The Rashtrapati Bhavan was known as the ______ during British rule.
Mark true or false: (a) Akbar entered into matrimonial alliances with Rajput rulers. (b) Aurangzeb continued Akbar's policy of liberalism.
Fill in the blanks: (a) Guru Gobind Singh founded the ______ and fixed the vow of five Ks. (b) ______ worship fire and believe in good and bad.
Match two items given in Column A with Column B (the rest are distracters): Gurmukhi script – Guru Arjan Dev; Khanqah – Sufis; Pahul – Sikhs; Ibadat Khana – Fatehpur Sikri. Pick two pairs.
questions.answer: Gurmukhi script was standardised by Guru Arjan Dev; the Ibadat Khana was at Fatehpur Sikri where Akbar held debates.

questions.q: Answer in a phrase: (a) Which Muslim poet was a devotee of Lord Krishna? (b) In which language did Namdev write?
Mark true or false: (a) Kabir was a disciple of Ramananda. (b) Guru Nanak supported idol worship.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in about 25 words.

questions.q: Examine the religious beliefs of the Sufis.
questions.answer: Sufis believed in the unity of God and of all religions, the equality of all human beings, love and self-surrender to God through a pir; they preached piety, tolerance and sympathy and used poetry and music (sama) to reach ecstasy.

questions.q: How did Humayun and Akbar promote the art of painting?
questions.answer: Humayun brought the Persian painters Mir Sayid Ali and Abdus Samad, who illustrated manuscripts like the Dastan-e-Amir Hamza; Akbar employed many Hindu painters such as Daswant and Basawan, leading to a fusion of Persian and Indian styles.

questions.q: Give two reasons why Aurangzeb stopped patronising music and painting.
questions.answer: He held orthodox views and was preoccupied with political problems and wars.

questions.q: Why were karkhanas important in medieval India?
questions.answer: The royal karkhanas employed artisans to produce luxury goods used by the court and also exported abroad, and they supported crafts and trade.

questions.q: What did Guru Arjan Dev give to the Sikhs?
questions.answer: The Adi Granth (containing the sayings of five gurus and saints), the standardised Gurmukhi script, and the site and foundation of the Har Mandir Sahib (Golden Temple) and Akal Takht at Amritsar.

questions.q: Name two famous Chishti Sufi saints and two folk dances of medieval India.
questions.answer: Moinuddin Chishti and Nizamuddin Auliya; Garba and Bhangra (also Giddha, Lavani).

questions.q: What was the speciality of the Hindustani school of music?
questions.answer: It produced sweet and rapturous melodies for different moods; ragas and raginis were personified; khayal, thumri and ghazal developed, with Tansen as pioneer.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 40–50 words.

questions.q: Explain the main features of the Bhakti movement.
questions.answer: Oneness of God and brotherhood of all human beings without discrimination of caste or gender; surrender to God, who is all-pervasive; intense personal devotion with a good moral life; the guru as spiritual guide with the pahul system; condemned rituals and sacrifices and used local languages.
questions.note: April 2022 (8 marks) asked for the development of the Bhakti movement.

questions.q: Describe the Mughal gardens and say why the Mughals built them.
questions.answer: The Mughals loved nature and built gardens with waterways, fountains and terraces, with water cascading from stage to stage with lamps behind it: Shalimar Bagh and Nishat Bagh in Kashmir, the three-stage Shalimar garden of Lahore and the seven-stage Pinjore garden near Chandigarh; the British copied them at Rashtrapati Bhavan and Vrindavan Gardens at Mysore.

questions.q: Analyse the religious and social reform among the Parsis / Zoroastrianism.
questions.answer: Zoroastrianism was founded by Zarathushtra in the 8th century BC in Persia: worship of fire, Ahura Mazda (good) and Ahura Man (evil), kindness and charity (Zend Avesta). Parsis settled at Navsari in Gujarat; reform started among them in Mumbai in the mid-19th century; leaders include Dadabhai Naoroji and Jamshedji Tata; they set up many charities.

questions.q: Write a note on Akbar's contribution to Indian culture.
questions.answer: Akbar fostered harmony by discouraging racial and religious bias, married Rajput princesses, unified the country with a central government, patronised art, architecture and learning, started Din-i-Illahi and held debates at the Ibadat Khana; his court had nine Navratnas such as Tansen and Todar Mal.

questions.q: Describe the life of people under the Delhi Sultanate.
questions.answer: Society consisted of aristocrats, priests, town people and peasants; trade flourished with Delhi as centre and the silver tanka as currency; caste was rigid but Hindus and Muslims exchanged customs in food, dress and music; Islam's equality led to the Bhakti and Sufi movements.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 150–200 words.

questions.q: Examine the development of music during the medieval period.
questions.answer: Under the Turko-Afghan rulers a synthesis of Indo-Iranian music began and developed further under the Mughals. Akbar, Jahangir and Shah Jahan patronised musicians; Tansen of Akbar's court sang classical ragas and composed new ones; Shah Jahan was a good singer. Aurangzeb disliked music, yet the largest number of Persian books on classical Indian music were written in his time. The Hindustani school arose in the north with sweet melodies for moods, personified ragas and raginis, and khayal, thumri and ghazal; the Carnatic school developed in the south. Sufis used sama and Bhakti saints sang geet and qawali, and ordinary people kept folk songs about local heroes like Alha-Udal and Dulla Bhatti.

questions.q: Explain the development of the Bhakti movement and its role in enriching Indian culture.
questions.answer: Islam's message of equality challenged the rigid caste society and gave rise to the Bhakti movement (14th–16th centuries). Saints from Alvars and Nayanars in the south, Ramanuja, Ramananda, Kabir, Nanak, Chaitanya, Mirabai, Namdev, Tulsidas and Surdas taught the oneness of God, devotion over ritual, equality and brotherhood. It split into nirguna and saguna streams. Their poetry in local languages (geet, qawali) united people and stimulated regional languages; Sikhism grew out of its nirguna branch.

questions.q: Describe Mughal painting and its development from Humayun to Aurangzeb.
questions.answer: Humayun brought Persian painters (Mir Sayid Ali, Abdus Samad) who nurtured manuscript painting such as Dastan-e-Amir Hamza with about 1200 paintings. Akbar employed Hindu painters like Daswant and Basawan and Persian and Indian styles fused. Under Jahangir, a painter himself with Ustad, Abul Hasan and Mansur, Mughal painting reached its zenith; landscapes, portraits and miniatures developed and artists signed works and got monthly salaries. Aurangzeb withdrew patronage, but Rajput and Pahari schools flourished under princes and the rich.

questions.q: Describe the rise of Sikhism and the contributions of Guru Nanak, Guru Arjan Dev and Guru Gobind Singh.
questions.answer: Sikhism was founded by Guru Nanak, a Khatri born at Talwandi who denounced idols, pilgrimages and rituals, preached one formless God, equality and purity of conduct, and sang hymns with the rabab. The fifth guru, Arjan Dev, gave the Adi Granth, the Gurmukhi script and the Golden Temple site at Amritsar with the Akal Takht. The tenth, Gobind Singh, created the Khalsa in 1699 with the five Ks (kesh, kangha, kada, kirpan, kachha) and made the Adi Granth the guru.
